## tsa04-p01
Therein, when one gradually refines thought for entry into the just-stated nature, then the contemplation-course preceded by true reasoning, good scripture, and good teacher-teaching has use. (4.1) For thus: by thought-force alone beings conceive the self as bound; that conceit is saṃsāra's block-cause. Hence adversarial-formed thought, arisen, shatters the saṃsāra-causing thought — hence cause of rise. (4.2) And it is of such form: than all limited-natured Śiva-ending principles, what is transcended — unlimited-consciousness-only-natured — that itself is the ultimate; that is thing-order-ground; that is the universe's vigor; through it lives the universe; that itself am I; hence universe-transcending and universe-self am I — thus. (4.3) And it does not arise for the Māyā-blind, from absence of true reasoning and the rest. (4.4) For Vaiṣṇavas and the rest are confined by passion-principle in so-much scripture — hence they do not face even toward higher vision. Hence they are haters of true-reasoning-good-scripture-good-teacher-teaching indeed. (4.5) As stated in the Lord's [scripture]: "Vaiṣṇavas and the rest, all of them, dyed by learning-passion, (4.6) do not find the supreme reality, devoid of omniscient knowledge." (4.7) Hence pierced by firm Śāmbhava descent alone, by good-scripture course, having refined thought, they enter the supreme nature. (4.8) "But thus would the supreme reality be thought-formed?" — Not so: for thought, fulfillment lies merely in shattering duality-habitation; but the supreme reality, everywhere in all forms, is self-shining itself. Hence therein thought serves neither for aiding nor refuting anything. (4.9) Therein, for one pierced by very firm descent, by itself, as self-perfected, rises true reasoning — which is called Goddess-initiated. (4.10) For others it is by scripture course — etcetera, in full in the descent-manifestation we shall teach. (4.11) But the teacher's function is in scripture-expounding; and scripture's function is in the rise of fitting thought born of unhesitating homogeneous connected text-study. Such thought-course alone is called true reasoning; and it alone is called contemplation — since, through making manifest by rendering brilliant what, though real, is unmanifest as if unreal, it is contemplated by which. (4.12) Nor here, apart from true reasoning of pure-knowledge-light-nature, is any other yoga-limb a direct means — of austerity and the rest, of the restraint class, of non-harm and the rest, of the yama kind, of filling and the rest, of the breath-control class — since concerned with knowable only: what function in consciousness? (4.13) Withdrawal too would merely heighten the sense-ground. Meditation, concentration, absorptions too, performed in practice-course in due order, would grant the meditator identity with the meditated thing. (4.14) And practice in the supreme principle, in Śiva-self, in own nature, is not possible at all. (4.15) For practice, of one rooted in consciousness, of the form of fixing breath-intellect-body, is like bundle-carrying, scripture-teaching, dance-practice; but in consciousness-nature there is nothing to take, nothing to remove — so how is there practice? (4.16) "What even by reasoning?" — if asked: here, it was stated that this is merely the manner of removing duality-habitation, not anything else. (4.17)"
l2_text:
## tsa04-p01 — thought washing thought
When you start refining thought itself, to walk into the nature just described, the old toolkit — true reasoning, good books, a good teacher's word — finally earns its keep. Here's why. Beings tie themselves up with nothing but thought-force: "I am bound." That knot is saṃsāra's lock. So let a counter-thought rise that eats the binding thought, and you have the cause of rising. Its shape: beyond every limited principle down to Śiva himself lies something unbordered — bare unlimited awareness. That is the ultimate. That is where things stand. That is the sap of the world — the world lives off it. That is I: past the world and made of it, both. The Māyā-blind don't get this thought — they lack true reasoning and the rest. The Vaiṣṇavas and company are fenced inside their own books' passion-principle; they won't even face uphill, and hate the reasoning, books, and teachers that would turn them. Their own books say it: dyed with learning's dye, they miss the supreme, void of all-knowing knowledge. Only those pierced by Śambhu's firm descent, refining thought through the good old course, walk into supreme nature. "But doesn't that make the supreme a thought?" No — thought's whole job is wrecking the habit of twoness; the supreme shines, everywhere, in every shape, by itself. Thought there neither helps nor refutes. For the deeply pierced, true reasoning rises on its own, fully formed — that is what "initiated by the Goddess" means. Others come by the book-route (the descent-chapters will spell it out). The teacher's business is expounding books; the books' business is growing the right thoughts in ungrudging, thorough study. That grown thought is true reasoning — and it is contemplation too: making the dim brilliant, showing the real as if never seen. No other yoga-limb is a straight means apart from this bright knowing — not sweat, not rules, not harmlessness and its vows, not breath-counting: those handle knowables, and what do knowables do for awareness? Breath-holds tune the senses. Sitting and its cousins, duly practised, deliver the sitter into the shape of whatever he sat on. But practice, in the supreme, in Śiva, in your own nature? Impossible. Practice means pinning breath, mind, body down — like drill with packs, lessons, dances. In awareness there's nothing to pick up and nothing to sweep out — so what would practice be? "Then what does reasoning do?" Just this, as said: it clears the squat of twoness. Nothing more.

c1.body:
When one gradually refines thought for entry into the nature just stated, the contemplation-course preceded by true reasoning, good scripture, and good teacher-teaching has use. Thought-force alone binds beings (the conceit "I am bound" is saṃsāra's lock); adversarial thought shatters it — that is the cause of rising. The adversarial thought's form: transcending all limited Śiva-ending principles is unlimited consciousness-only — the ultimate, thing-order-ground, universe's vigor, "I am" (universe-transcending and universe-self). It does not arise for the Māyā-blind (no true reasoning). Vaiṣṇavas are confined by passion-principle in their scripture and hate the reasoning that would turn them (scripture quote). Only Śāmbhava-firm-descent-pierced enter by good-scripture course. The objection "would this make the supreme thought-formed?" is dissolved: thought's fulfillment is merely shattering duality-habitation; the supreme self-shines everywhere — thought neither aids nor refutes. For the very-firmly-pierced, true reasoning rises spontaneously — "Goddess-initiated." Others come by scripture-course (details later). The teacher expounds scripture; scripture raises fitting thought born of unhesitating study — that is true reasoning, and it is contemplation (making the dim brilliant). No other yoga-limb is a direct means (austerity, restraint, non-harm, yama, filling, breath-control handle knowables, not consciousness). Withdrawal heightens senses; meditation/concentration/absorption grant object-identity. Practice in the supreme nature is impossible (bundle-carrying analogy; in awareness there is nothing to take or remove). Reasoning's sole job: removing duality-habitation.

The passage moves in seven steps. (1) Bondage-conceit and its shattering. (2) The ultimate formula (unlimited consciousness-only). (3) Vaiṣṇava fence + quote. (4) Goddess-initiated spontaneous reasoning vs scripture course. (5) Teacher/scripture division. (6) Yoga-limb demotion (tapaḥ/restraint/yama/breath handle knowables; pratyāhāra heightens senses; dhyāna grants identity). (7) Practice-impossibility (bundle analogy; nothing to take/remove) + tarka's sole job (removing duality-habitation) + worldly practice parallel.

## tsa04-p02
"Even in worldly practice, making manifest the liked form of this and that body etc. as consciousness-self, and disfavoring other forms — this alone is the point of practice. (4.18) But in the supreme principle, as stated, there is nothing to reject. (4.19) Duality-habitation too, though called so, is no separate thing-entity, but mere non-recognition of nature — hence it was stated that duality-removal is done by thought. (4.20) This ultimate: nature shining, in non-recognition-nature grasped by itself through autonomy, gradually abandoned — about-to-bloom, then blooming, then bloomed — by this course shines forth; and such shining too is the Lord's nature itself. Hence here the yoga-limbs are not direct means. (4.21) Reasoning too — even graced — true reasoning alone is therein the direct means. And it is pure knowledge; and refined manifoldly it comes to be — namely: sacrifice, fire-offering, muttering, vow, yoga. Therein, for establishing thought that all things abide in the Lord alone, that nothing distinct exists: offering all things into the Lord is sacrifice. And since, through loveliness, those who themselves resort to consciousness-entry find offering into the Lord easy — with that intent, outer use of lovely flowers, libations, scents and the rest was stated. (4.22) For obtaining rooted thought that all things are Lord-fire-made: in the Lord-consciousness-fire's glow, with intent of relishing the swallowing of all things, dissolving all things leaving fire-mass alone, is fire-offering. (4.23) Likewise, for the rise of both-natured grasping, regardless of outer-inner-and-rest object-natured distinct things: inner grasping that 'that supreme reality is own-nature-become' is muttering. (4.24) For gaining, everywhere always, the conceit of the means-less Lord, by conceit of Lord-sameness, seeing even of body and of pot and the rest, is vow. (4.25) As stated in Śrī Nandiśikhā: 'All-sameness is the supreme vow.' (4.26) Thus by varied pure-knowledge-portion thoughts, when the thought-free natural ultimate reality shines, abiding in its manifestation-form alone is yoga. (4.27) Therein the Lord, full-consciousness-natured — his fullness itself is power: clan, capability, wave, heart, essence, throb, glory, triple-peak, Kālī, attractor, Caṇḍī, speech, enjoyment, sight, eternal, and so on, by āgama-tongues proceeding by respective etymology, is named — by that form may he abide in meditators' hearts. (4.28) And she, seen with total-power-regard, shines as fullness-conviction. (4.29) And his powers are countless. (4.30) What need of much: whatever is universe, they are his powers — how could they be taught? (4.31) Of three, so far, the universe is completed: by which, as undivided-consciousness-only-nature, bearing, seeing, shining, from Śiva to earth, the Lord upholds — that is his glorious supreme power. (4.32) And by which, as mirror-elephant-like, by difference-nondifference, that is his glorious supreme-nonsupreme power. (4.33)"
l2_text:
## tsa04-p02 — the rites go inward
Even ordinary drill proves the point: you picture the body you want as awareness itself and un-picture the rest — that is all practice ever was. In the supreme there's nothing to throw away — said already. And the "dwelling in twoness" isn't some separate thing either; it's just nature not recognizing itself. So thought clears it — as stated. The ultimate works like this: nature shining, grasped by itself in freedom, sheds unknowing bit by bit — budding, blooming, bloomed — and shines out in that order. That shining is the Lord's own nature too. So no yoga-limbs as straight means here. Reasoning — graced reasoning — is the straight means: bright knowing itself. Refined many ways, it wears five shapes: sacrifice, fire-giving, inward saying, vow, and yoga. Sacrifice: to settle the thought that everything stands in the Lord and nothing stands apart — give everything to the Lord; and since the lovely-minded enter awareness on their own, lovely flowers and scents outside were prescribed to make giving easy. Fire-giving: to root the thought that all things are Lord-fire — relish swallowing everything into that fire until only fire-mass is left. Inward saying: to birth two-sided grasping — hold "that supreme is my own nature" inside, whatever the object. Vow: to win the conceit of the Lord who needs no means, always, everywhere — look at body and pot alike as his equals (Nandiśikhā: all-sameness is the supreme vow). So through these motley shards of bright knowing, when the thoughtless natural ultimate shines, staying in that shining is yoga. The Lord is full awareness; his fullness is power — clan, might, wave, heart, pith, throb, glory, triple-peak, Kālī, dragger, Fierce, Speech, enjoyment, sight, the ever-fresh — the books call him by whatever name fits, so he may dwell in meditators' hearts. Seen whole-powered, that fullness shines as conviction. His powers? Past counting — whatever the universe is, they are; who could teach them? Three contain it: the Supreme power, holding-seeing-shining everything from Śiva to earth as bare awareness; the half-and-half, mirror-and-elephant-wise, in difference-and-not; the lower, in mutually fenced-apart difference. And the embrace that swallows all three back into itself, recollecting inward — that is goddess Parā herself, also called Mother-of-Beings, Time's Dragger, and the rest.

c1.body:
Even ordinary practice proves the point: you picture the liked form as awareness and un-picture the rest — that is all practice ever was. In the supreme there is nothing to reject (duality-habitation is mere non-recognition, not a separate entity). The ultimate shines forth by stages (budding → blooming → bloomed); that shining is the Lord's nature. So no yoga-limbs as straight means. True reasoning — graced reasoning — is the straight means: pure knowledge, refined manifoldly into five shapes: sacrifice (offering all into the Lord — outer flowers for the lovely-minded), fire-offering (dissolving all into Lord-fire), muttering (inner grasping "that supreme is own-nature"), vow (seeing body/pot with Lord-identity; Nandiśikhā: all-sameness = supreme vow), yoga (staying in the shining). The Lord is full awareness; his fullness is power — clan, might, wave, heart, pith, throb, glory, triple-peak, Kālī, dragger, Fierce, Speech, enjoyment, sight, ever-fresh — named by āgama-tongues. Seen whole-powered, that fullness shines as conviction. His powers are past counting. Three contain it: supreme power (holding-seeing-shining everything from Śiva to earth as bare awareness), supreme-nonsupreme (mirror-elephant, difference-nondifference), nonsupreme (mutually fenced-apart difference). The embrace that swallows all three back into itself, recollecting inward, is goddess Parā herself (Mātṛsadbhāva, Kālakarṣiṇī).

The passage has two movements. First, the revaluation: ordinary practice = picturing liked forms as awareness; in the supreme, nothing to reject; duality-habitation = non-recognition; the ultimate shines by stages; no yoga-limbs as straight means; true reasoning is the straight means (pure knowledge), refined into five shapes with their intents (sacrifice: offering all into the Lord; fire-offering: dissolving all into Lord-fire; muttering: inner grasping; vow: Lord-identity seeing; yoga: staying in the shining). Second, the three powers: the Lord is full awareness named by āgama-tongues; three contain it (parā/parāpara/aparā); the holder is Parā herself.

## tsa04-p03
"[Continuation: 4.34] By which, with mutually separate selfhood, by difference alone, that is his glorious nonsupreme power. (4.34) The holder that, by self-embrace, swallows the threefold through recollecting-turned-inward, is his goddess Parā herself — named by other words like glorious Mātṛsadbhāva, Kālakarṣiṇī. (4.35) These four powers, through autonomy, each proceed threefold. (4.36) In creation, maintenance, and dissolution — thus they become twelve. (4.37) As: consciousness first grasps a thing inwardly, then outwardly too, manifestly grasps it, grasping affection there, then grasps that same thing wanting re-absorption inward, then makes and swallows the doubt obstructing re-absorption, grasps in the self, by re-absorption, the thing-portion with swallowed-doubt-portion, grasps even 'my consumer-nature is this form' as own nature, grasps in consumer-nature-grasping the abiding of some thing as trace, of another as consciousness-only-remainder, grasps the sense-wheel by sole consequentiality of nature-grasping, grasps even the sense-lord, grasps even the imagined Māyā-knower-form, grasps even the knower relishing contraction-to-expansion-grasp, hence grasps even the expanded form — thus these twelve goddess consciousnesses, aiming at knowers one or many, partaking in rise simultaneously, in course, in twos, threes and so on, revolving wheel-like, shining outward too in month-fortnight-heap order down to pot-cloth order, nourishing the wheel-lord's autonomy, are called by the word Śrī Kālī. (4.38) And grasping is motion, throwing, knowing, counting, enjoying, sounding, dissolving into self. (4.39) As the venerable Bhūtirāja teachers said: 'From throwing, from knowing, Kālī — through grasping-power.' (4.40) And this sense is to be seen expanded here and there in my composed exposition, treatise, hymn and the rest. (4.41) Neither is the over-secret to be proclaimed in one place, nor ever to be hidden — so indeed our teachers. (4.42) Thus what was called sacrifice-offering-and-the-rest is to be regarded in Maheśvara of such kind. (4.43) For all, from Viṣṇu to Śiva, see the rejectable itself as adoptable-ground-nature — and that is false view, necessarily to be abandoned by unsurpassed yogins. For that very purpose is the great zeal of the Lord of Knowledge in the Experience-Hymn. In such sacrifice-to-yoga pentads, in each manifold establishment — as it comes to be, so one should practice — not by food-inedible-purity-impurity discrimination, of thing-nature-abandoned, mere-imagination-essenced, should the self be wearied. As stated first: purity is not thing-nature, like blueness — elsewhere, of that same, impurity is enjoined; as of giving, in initiatedness it is enjoined: 'for him that is impure there' — if so, in another injunction likewise; 'the other injunction is unreal, since sublated' — if so: no — sublation by Śiva-command alone is reasonable, proven by reasoning and by endless-āgama establishment beginning with Sarvajñānottara — as we shall teach. (4.44) Hence from Vedic onward, even Pārameśvara-Siddhānta-Tantra-Kula-Ucchuṣma-śāstra-taught restraint, prescription, or prohibition is here effective to the extent of nothing — it is established. ## tsa04-p03 — twelve goddesses, and how to live
Four powers, each going three — twelve, for creating, keeping, unmaking. Watch awareness do it: take a thing in, show it out, warm to it, want it back in, breed the doubt that blocks return, eat the doubt, hold the thing-minus-doubt in yourself, note "my consumer-nature is this," let one trace linger as habit and another dissolve to bare awareness, raise the sense-wheel, raise its lords, raise the dreamt Māyā-knower, raise the knower who likes tightening into opening, raise the opened shape — twelve goddess-awarenesses, aimed at one knower or many, together or in turn, in twos and threes, wheeling like seasons, months, heaps, down to pots and cloths, feeding the wheel-lord's freedom: Kālīs, every one. "Grasping" means going, throwing, knowing, counting, enjoying, sounding, melting into self (old Bhūtirāja masters: "from throwing, from knowing — Kālī — by grasping-power"). The full sense lives spread through my longer works and hymns — look there. And the teachers' rule: don't shout the deepest anywhere, don't bury it either. So "sacrifice and the rest" means: in a Maheśvara like this. Everyone from Viṣṇu to Śiva treats the rejectable as the ground to take — false sight, drop it if you're beyond compare (the Experience-Hymn's whole fire is for this). In these fives from rite to yoga, each richly settled — live them as settled, not by edible-inedible, pure-impure checklists: those tire a self over thought-made rules abandoned by things themselves. Purity isn't in things the way blue is — the same act is foul elsewhere, enjoined here. "Giving counts as pure only for the initiated — elsewhere the same giving is foul, so all injunctions wobble"? No: Śiva's word alone overrides — reasoned out and settled by endless revelation from Sarvajñānottara on (full case later). So from Veda down through Pārameśvara, Siddhānta, Tantra, Kula, Ucchuṣma — every rule, order, and ban laid down there does exactly nothing here. Established.

c1.body:
Four powers, each going threefold (autonomy) = twelve, for creating, keeping, unmaking. The kalana demonstration: awareness grasps inward, then outward, affection, re-absorption-will, doubt-making-and-swallowing, consumer-nature, vessel-traces, sense-wheel, sense-lords, Māyā-knower, contracted-then-expanding knower, expanded form — twelve goddess-consciousnesses, aimed at one or many, together or in turn, revolving like seasons, nourishing wheel-lord autonomy = Kālīs. Kalana = motion/throwing/knowing/counting/enjoying/sounding/self-dissolving (Bhūtirāja quote). The full sense lives in the author's longer works (vivaraṇa/prakaraṇa/stotra); neither blab everywhere nor hide totally (teachers' rule). So "sacrifice and the rest" means: in a Maheśvara like this. All from Viṣṇu to Śiva treat the rejectable as adoptable-ground — false view, must be dropped by unsurpassed yogins (Anubhavastotra's zeal). In yāga-to-yoga pentads each manifoldly established — practice as established, not by food/purity discriminations (impurity isn't thing-nature like blue; Śiva-command alone overrides, proven by reason + endless āgamas — Tantrāloka for detail). Vedic-to-Kula rules alike do nothing here.

The passage has two movements. First, the twelve-Kālī demonstration: four powers × threefold = twelve, with the full kalana sequence (grasping inward → outward → affection → re-absorption → doubt → consumer → vessel → sense-wheel → sense-lords → Māyā-knower → contracted/expanding → expanded). Second, the conduct rule: kalana = motion/knowing/enjoying (Bhūtirāja); teachers' secrecy rule; "sacrifice and the rest" = in a Maheśvara; false view (rejectable as adoptable); Anubhavastotra's zeal; purity is not thing-nature (blue analogy); Śiva-command overrides (reason + endless āgamas); Tantrāloka for detail; Vedic-to-Kula rules ineffective.
